features.name: River Marle
features.notes: Rises on the north face of the Carrodan Range, crosses the Ansel Plain north-west, and cuts north through the Kennoch Heights in a gorge to the Hern Sea. The paint shows its water on the plain and its lower course as a cleft in the mountains. Known to: the Sarrow; plainsfolk.

features.name: River Morrow
features.notes: Slow and winding through the western forest to the north shore of the gulf. Known to: god-healing's people along its lower course.

features.name: River Alder
features.notes: The long gulf river: from the south face of the Kennoch Heights across the Aldermark to the head of the gulf. Known to: the Aldermark; the player's people (its lower course).

features.name: Hollin Water
features.notes: Feeder of the River Alder from the foot of the Carrodan Range.

features.name: River Cand
features.notes: The middle gulf river, from the plain south-west of Whitmoor to the delta.

features.name: River Rudd
features.notes: From the west foot of the Hask Ridge across the Cander Plain, past the north end of the Rudd Hills, to the delta.

features.name: River Ellow
features.notes: From the south end of the Hask Ridge south to the Lome Sea, with one wide bend under stony hills.

features.name: River Wellen
features.notes: From the Drymarch through the Wellen Hills into the Braidwater, where it parts into many channels.

features.name: Tawnwater
features.notes: From the east foot of the Hask Ridge south-east through the Wellen Hills to the Braidwater's delta.

features.name: River Farrow
features.notes: From the Ossenwold east and south-east across the Farrow Grass to its estuary on the Corrith Coast. Other painted streams of the grass are not traced.

features.name: River Iss
features.notes: A short river from the east end of the Carrodan Range north to the Hern Sea, slow and bending in its lower course.

features.name: Wellen Brook
features.notes: A spring stream from the Wellen Hills to the River Wellen. Data only, smaller than the sheet paints.

features.name: unnamed town
features.notes: The player's people's home, about 5,000, on the old clay levee where the track meets the main channel; left unnamed by the player for play. A market, a house with a poor hall, a drum on the bank.

features.name: Bank Way
features.notes: The worn track along the top of the old levee through the unnamed town.

features.name: Maun Flats
features.notes: Salt flats on the seaward side of the delta, pale and white-crusted; salt pans worked by the town's rakers. Nearest listed type; they are tidal flats, not marsh.

features.name: Old Rudd Way
features.notes: An old built road from the delta's head east over the Pellow Downs into the Rudd Hills, sunken and grassed over in stretches. Older than the town.

features.name: Alder Road
features.notes: The Aldermark's road down the River Alder to the head of the delta, where the Bank Way takes it on.

features.name: Ruddfold
features.notes: A village of hill folk in the Rudd Hills, ore diggers and charcoal burners, kin to the town's hill people.

features.name: Pellow Vaults
features.notes: Sealed vaults of the vanished trading power in the low downs, beside the Old Rudd Way. Known to: the town, as a story.

features.name: Maun Stair
features.notes: The old trading power's sea-door on the gulf shore east of the delta: drowned steps and a broken quay.

features.name: unnamed harbor town
features.notes: god-sea's people's home, about 2,000, a walled harbor town; left unnamed by its god for play.

features.name: Garrow Skerries
features.notes: Skerries off the shore. Nearest listed type: a scatter of sea rocks.

features.name: Cliff of Bones
features.notes: Enormous bones in a sea cliff, uncovered by the tide.

features.name: Drowned Causeway
features.notes: An old road running out under the water from the shore.

features.name: unnamed walled town
features.notes: god-secrets's people's home, about 5,000, earth and timber walls on firm ground inside the bend of the River Iss; left unnamed for play. Many times rebuilt; cellars under cellars.

features.name: Iss Marsh
features.notes: Marsh along the lower River Iss to the sea.

features.name: Iss Track
features.notes: A worn track to the town's land gate.

features.name: Herd Road
features.notes: A trail beaten wide by herds and feet between the upland woods and the grass. The band's round of the year.

features.name: Ossen Mire
features.notes: Wet ground in a hollow below the wood's edge.

features.name: Ribhill
features.notes: A long curve of enormous bones under a hill on the grass, which the herds avoid.

features.name: unnamed spring town
features.notes: god-rivers's people's home, about 2,000, a walled town where Wellen Brook leaves the hills, a spring by its wall; left unnamed for play.

features.name: Brook Path
features.notes: A path worn down along Wellen Brook to the ford on the River Wellen.

features.name: Wellen Ford
features.notes: The ford and ferry where Wellen Brook meets the River Wellen.

features.name: Stopped Spring
features.notes: A sealed spring stopped with a great flat stone.

features.name: Dry Braid
features.notes: A stretch of buried dry riverbed within the Braidwater.

features.name: unnamed bend town
features.notes: god-dreams's people's home, about 3,000 within the wall, on the stony rise above the bend of the River Ellow; left unnamed for play.

features.name: Ellow Scar
features.notes: A quarry scar on the hillside above the bend.

features.name: Ellow Barrows
features.notes: Old graves made with great care, older than any family can name.

features.name: unnamed court steading
features.notes: The larger seat of god-healing's people, where the line and the court sit; the people, about 5,000, live in steadings along the lower River Morrow. Left unnamed for play.

features.name: Morrow Mounds
features.notes: A field of low old grave mounds on the river bank.

features.name: unnamed winter city
features.notes: The Sarrow's winter city, timber and fitted stone at the ford; about 4,000 within in the cold months, the host of about 18,000 wintering in the valley round it. Left unnamed for play.

features.name: Marle Ford
features.notes: The ford on the River Marle below the city, with a toll house.

features.name: Stair Pass
features.notes: The pass that comes down to the ford from the west, with steps cut in the rock.

features.name: Far Notch
features.notes: The pass that opens across the valley from Stair Pass, toward the plain.

features.name: Kennoch Gates
features.notes: Gates cut in a hillside on an old cut road, a toll place of a rule long ended.

features.name: Pass Road
features.notes: The old cut road through the heights by way of the ford, the way between the west and the north.

features.name: Aldermoot
features.notes: Chief city of the old river kingdom of the Aldermark, at the turn of the River Alder. A quarter of the slow long-memoried people, a few hundred, keeps its own law and books here.

features.name: Wenlow
features.notes: A river town of the Aldermark on the lower River Alder.

features.name: Haskhold
features.notes: Chief of the mining holds on the Hask Ridge, a stone town that sells iron.

features.name: Southhold of Hask
features.notes: A mining hold at the south end of the Hask Ridge.

features.name: Corrith
features.notes: Chief town of the harbor league, on the south coast.

features.name: Port Sennet
features.notes: A harbor town of the league.

features.name: Whitmoor Ring
features.notes: A ring of great standing stones about three miles across at the middle of Whitmoor. Data only, smaller than the sheet paints. The center point.

features.name: unnamed fallen stone
features.notes: A warm blue-grey stone, heavy for its size, that fell in the Bren Hills on the night the gods came down. No one has named it. Placed by r-0141 and r-0142.

features.name: Gannel Stones
features.notes: Added on Night 3b. Three standing stones on the open grass of the Hollin Reaches, north of Whitmoor: two uprights and a notched third behind them, a sightline on the star. Data only, smaller than the sheet paints. Known to: plainsfolk who pass; the Aldermark's chancery, as a line in an old survey roll.
